reasoning: The root cause is located in the procedure text itself (SKILL.md:52-53 never names the value of the token), the fix is the smallest one that closes it — one Group 0 clause, one ADDED planning requirement, one text test, no script — and every alternative that would have added a script or a flag is rejected in design.md D1 on a reason this review could check against create_tracking_issue.py.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 names three simpler-or-heavier alternatives and rejects each on a checkable reason: a duplicate guard in `create_tracking_issue` (no deterministic link from change to source issue — confirmed: #241's title is the change name `releases-through-auto-update`, not #199's title `Releases reach consumers through plugin auto-update`, and the proposal need not cite the issue, so any guard is a heuristic that can refuse a genuine first issue); an `--issue <N>` flag on the tail (a second carrier beside the token that `start_change.py:92` would still have to read from `tasks.md`, so the planner's choice only moves one step later); rewording the `area is set at creation` refusal (create_tracking_issue.py:58-64 — that branch is only reached when the token already carries a number, so it was never printed in the #199 run). The plan itself is already minimal: one edited sentence in SKILL.md, one 18-word sentence in `.claude/rules/workflow.md`, one requirement, one test; no script, no flag, no new file. The one further simplification available — deleting workflow.md's tracking-issue clause instead of correcting it, since that file's own header says it must not duplicate the contract — is pre-existing duplication and removing it would widen the diff (§VII surgical), so keeping the minimal correction is right.

map.evidence: The delta has exactly one scenario and tasks.md:27 maps it to two tests, both verified to exist or to be creatable where named: the first clause (Group 0 carries the number) → the new `tests/publisher/test_planning_workflow.py::test_plan_from_an_existing_issue`, which reads `_group0()` (test_planning_workflow.py:76-79, the slice `Group 0` … `Group 1` of the `## Tasks` section — the edited sentence at SKILL.md:52-53 is inside it); the second clause (`create_tracking_issue` creates no issue and moves that issue to `Planned`) → the existing `tests/publisher/test_start_change.py::test_existing_tracking_issue` (line 656, which loads `create_tracking_issue` there and asserts no create, area refused, `Planned` alone) — correctly named as unchanged, since this change alters no script. `scenario_coverage` is empty and that is right: no scenario of the delta is unprovable. Nit for the applying pass, not blocking: the THEN's second clause restates the already-specified scenario `planning` / Existing tracking issue (openspec/specs/planning/spec.md:123-125); trimming it to the first clause would leave the requirement's own observable outcome and no copy to keep in sync.

red.evidence: Group 1 (tasks.md:7) is RED-first and the RED is real, not vacuous: of the two asserted substrings, `tracking issue <N>` is in Group 0 today (SKILL.md:52) and `the number of the issue the change is planned from` is not, so the new test fails in its body before task 2.1 — no stub is needed since the subject is text, and `check_red.py` is run on the node id with the commit before the implementation. The implementation (2.1) lands in the group after, and the assertion strings match the replacement text of 2.1 character for character. No mapped test is left out of the RED run: the second mapped test is an existing green test of an untouched script.

platform.evidence: The plan rests on no new platform behaviour — no event, permission, merge rule, token scope or CLI flag is newly relied on — and the design says so by touching no script. What it rests on is an observed run, recorded as observation rather than inference in proposal.md:3-14 (2026-09-28: the tail ran `create_tracking_issue.py releases-through-auto-update --area Distribution` on a `tasks.md` still carrying the placeholder, #241 opened, #199 left in `Todo`, repaired by hand). This review checked the record against the live platform: `gh issue view` gives #199 CLOSED `Releases reach consumers through plugin auto-update`, #241 CLOSED `releases-through-auto-update` (the duplicate, titled from the proposal as create_tracking_issue.py:88-98 creates it), #242 OPEN, the issue this change is planned from, already a Project item in `Planned`. The repository behaviour the fix depends on is read in the code, not assumed: create_tracking_issue.py:57-67 takes the existing-issue branch on a numeric token, refuses `--area` and sets `Planned` alone, and start_change.py:56,92 reads the same token.

replaced.evidence: Nothing is replaced and no guard is dropped: design.md Non-Goals keep both scripts unchanged, proposal.md:38 records `Added: none. Removed: none. Scripts unchanged.`, and the only edits are two prose sentences plus one test. The token stays the single carrier of the number to both scripts (ADR 0027, cited in proposal.md:39-40 as standing rather than restated), so no input a script declares is swapped for one the caller supplies, and the `area is set at creation` refusal, the review-verdict gate and the `propose run not finished` refusal of `start_change` all keep their current meaning. The migration section is correspondingly one line (revert the PR, no state migrates), which is accurate.

catcher.evidence: The one catcher the plan names is in design.md Risks — if the planner still writes `<N>` for an issue-born change the duplicate is visible in the tail's own output — and it traces to a concrete step, not to a role: `create_tracking_issue.py:98` prints `ok: issue #<N> created, Planned, area <area>` on the create branch versus `ok: issue #<N> Planned` at line 67 on the existing-issue branch, so the run that should have been the second form prints a number the planner did not start from, and the source issue visibly stays out of `Planned`. The residual this leaves is stated rather than hidden: no later step refuses, because `start_change` then reads a token that is numeric and an issue that is `Planned`, so the duplicate passes the delivery gate — which is why the rule is placed in the very sentence the planner copies when it writes the token, and why the heuristic guard that could refuse was rejected in D1. Given the missing key (no deterministic change→issue link), that is the strongest catcher available and the plan does not claim more.

length.evidence: Every sentence the plan adds or edits, with its count against the words its tests assert. (1) SKILL.md Group 0 (tasks.md:11): 30 words, up from 19; the added clause is 12 words (`the number of the issue the change is planned from, else`) and the new test asserts 13 (`tracking issue <N>` = 3, `the number of the issue the change is planned from` = 10), so the added text is fully asserted; the unchanged remainder is held by test_planning_workflow.py:254 and :392 and by the `PLACEHOLDER` tests of test_start_change.py:60. (2) The ADDED requirement body (specs/planning/spec.md:4-5): 29 words, asserted by the same 13 words of the new test plus the existing-branch test; the only unasserted fragment is the timing `as it writes tasks.md` (4 words), which no text test can pin and which carries the rule's point. (3) The scenario (spec.md:8-9): ~30 words, first clause asserted by the new test, second by test_start_change.py:656-670. (4) `.claude/rules/workflow.md`: 18 words, 0 asserted — no test reads that file, and that is the repository norm rather than a gap of this plan: `.claude/rules/` is not distributed (SPARSE_PATHS, tests/publisher/test_plugin.py:151) and the contract it points at is the one SKILL.md carries and the tests assert. No explanation in parentheses, no `why` inside a rule, no clause the issue did not ask for.

bespoke.evidence: The plan adds no script and no check: proposal.md:35-38 lists only edits (SKILL.md, .claude/rules/workflow.md, tests/publisher/test_planning_workflow.py, and openspec/specs/planning/spec.md by archive) and design.md:31 states that the bespoke-check decision therefore does not apply — correct under the schema's requirement, since the class asks for a decision only for an added script or check. The pull toward a script was faced instead of ignored: D1's first alternative is exactly the guard a `scripts over instructions` reading would suggest, and it is rejected because there is no deterministic input to compute the answer from (the source issue exists only in the planner's own run, not in any artifact the script reads), which is the case where a gate can only guess. No ADR is added, with the reason on record (ADR 0027 stands; this change names who writes the number).
